literal: In the twelfth month, Minister of Works Hou Jing was made Minister of Education, and Secretariat Director Han Gui was made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hou Jing, minister of works, was made minister of education, and Han Gui, director of the secretariat, was made minister of works.

literal: On wuzi day, Grand Preceptor Sun Teng was made recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.
idiomatic: On wuzi day Sun Teng, grand preceptor, was made recorder of Masters of Writing affairs.

literal: That year Koguryo, Tuyuhun, and Rouran all sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Koguryo, Tuyuhun, and Rouran all sent envoys with tribute.

literal: In the fourth year, fifth month of summer, on renyin day, Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, on renyin day in the fifth month of summer, Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Sixth month, on gengzi day, Minister of Education Hou Jing was made grand mobile office of Henan to strike and defend as occasion demanded.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengzi day, Hou Jing, minister of education, was made grand mobile office of Henan to strike and defend as occasion demanded.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, on renyin day, Supernumerary Scattered Cavalier Attendant Yuan Kuo was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on renyin day, Yuan Kuo, supernumerary scattered cavalier attendant, was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan.

literal: Eighth month: the Han and Wei stone classics at Luoyang were moved to Ye.
idiomatic: In the eighth month the Han and Wei stone classics were moved from Luoyang to Ye.

literal: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu led his host west from Ye in campaign; Prince of Qi Wenxiang joined him at Jin province.
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu marched west from Ye; Prince of Qi Wenxiang joined him at Jin province.

literal: Ninth month: they besieged Yubi to provoke battle; Baoju and Hei La did not dare respond.
idiomatic: In the ninth month they besieged Yubi to provoke battle; Baoju and Hei La did not dare respond.

literal: Eleventh month of winter: Duke Xianwu of Qi fell ill and the army withdrew.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Duke Xianwu of Qi fell ill and the army withdrew.

literal: Prince Wenxiang went to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang went to Jinyang.

literal: That year Shiwei, Wuji, Dudouyu, Koguryo, and Rouran all sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Shiwei, Wuji, Dudouyu, Koguryo, and Rouran all sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Seventh month of autumn, on wuxu day, an edict posthumously granted the king the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the full rites of the Nine Bestowals; his posthumous title was Duke Xianwu.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on wuxu day, an edict posthumously granted the king the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the full rites of the nine bestowals; his posthumous title was Duke Xianwu.

literal: Prince of Qi Wenxiang was made commissioner with full powers, grand chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and Prince of Bohai.
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Wenxiang was made commissioner with full powers, grand chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and prince of Bohai.

literal: On renyin day an edict ordered the prince to oversee state and military affairs; a palace envoy was sent to urge him earnestly.
idiomatic: On renyin day an edict ordered the prince to oversee state and military affairs, and a palace envoy was sent to urge him earnestly.

literal: [22] Eighth month: Prince of Qi Wenxiang entered court and firmly declined the chancellorship; an edict again appointed him grand general, the rest remaining as before.
idiomatic: [22] In the eighth month Prince of Qi Wenxiang entered court and firmly declined the chancellorship; an edict again appointed him grand general, with all else unchanged.

literal: On jiashen day Duke Xianwu of Qi was buried northwest of Ye city; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.
idiomatic: On jiashen day Duke Xianwu of Qi was buried northwest of Ye; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.

literal: Ninth month: Prince Wenxiang returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Prince Wenxiang returned to Jinyang.

literal: On xinyou day Xiao Yan sent his elder brother's son Marquis Yuanming of Zhenyang to lead troops against Xuzhou, dam the Si River at Cold Mountain, and flood Pengcheng to coordinate with Hou Jing.
idiomatic: On xinyou day Xiao Yan sent his nephew Marquis Yuanming of Zhenyang to raid Xuzhou, dam the Si at Cold Mountain, flood Pengcheng, and coordinate with Hou Jing.

literal: Tenth month of winter, on yiyou day, Murong Shaozong, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand mobile office of the southeast route; together with Grand General of Agile Cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and grand commander Gao Yue and Pan Xiangle he campaigned against Yuanming.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on yiyou day, Murong Shaozong, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand mobile office of the southeast route; with Gao Yue, grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the three excellencies and grand commander, and Pan Xiangle he attacked Yuanming.

literal: Eleventh month: they inflicted a great defeat, captured Yuanming and his two sons Yu and Dao, more than two hundred commanders, took and slew fifty thousand, and those who died of cold, exhaustion, or drowning were beyond count.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month they routed the enemy, captured Yuanming and his sons Yu and Dao, more than two hundred commanders, and killed or captured fifty thousand; countless others died of cold, exhaustion, or drowning.

literal: Twelfth month, on yihai day, Xiao Yuanming reached the capital; the emperor received him at Changhe Gate, rebuked him, and pardoned him.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai day, Xiao Yuanming reached the capital; the emperor met him at Changhe Gate, rebuked him, and pardoned him.

literal: Yue and the others turned their army to campaign against Hou Jing.
idiomatic: Yue and the others turned their army against Hou Jing.

literal: That year Koguryo and Wuji both sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Koguryo and Wuji both sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Spring, first month of the sixth year, on jihai day, Grand Commander Gao Yue and others at Woyang greatly defeated Hou Jing, capturing and slaying more than fifty thousand; the rest drowned in the Wo River until the water would not flow.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, on jihai day, Gao Yue and others at Woyang crushed Hou Jing, killing or capturing more than fifty thousand; the rest drowned in the Wo River until it would not flow.

literal: Jing fled to Huainan.
idiomatic: Jing fled to Huainan.

literal: On jiwei day Prince of Qi Wenxiang came to court and asked that captives taken at Cold Mountain be granted to the hundred offices and supervising generals in graded shares.
idiomatic: On jiwei day Prince of Qi Wenxiang came to court and asked that captives from Cold Mountain be granted to officials and generals in graded shares.

literal: Second month, on jimao day, Xiao Yan sent envoys suing at the gate for peace and also sent a letter of condolence to Prince of Qi Wenxiang.
idiomatic: In the second month, on jimao day, Xiao Yan sent envoys suing for peace at the gate and a letter of condolence to Prince of Qi Wenxiang.

literal: Prince Wenxiang returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang returned to Jinyang.

literal: Third month, on guisi day, Xu, grand preceptor and prince of Xiangcheng, was made grand marshal; Gao Yue, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies with open office, was made grand preceptor.
idiomatic: In the third month, on guisi day, Xu, grand preceptor and prince of Xiangcheng, was made grand marshal; Gao Yue, equal in honor to the three excellencies with open office, was made grand preceptor.

literal: On xinhai day, because of severe drought through winter and spring, criminals were pardoned in graded measure.
idiomatic: On xinhai day, because of severe drought through winter and spring, criminals were pardoned in graded measure.

literal: Fourth month of summer, on jiazi day, Masters of Writing clerks Zhang Yonghe of the Ministry of Personnel and Cui Kuo of Qing province and others falsely assumed offices; when the affair was exposed and investigated, those implicated numbered more than sixty thousand.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi day, Zhang Yonghe, a Ministry of Personnel clerk, Cui Kuo of Qing province, and others had falsely assumed offices; when the affair was exposed, more than sixty thousand were implicated.

literal: [23] Eighth month of autumn, on jiaxu day, Murong Shaozong, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand mobile office; together with Grand Preceptor Gao Yue, Minister of Education Han Gui, Grand Commander Liu Feng, and others he campaigned against Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan and led the Wei River to flood the city.
idiomatic: [23] In the eighth month of autumn, on jiaxu day, Murong Shaozong, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand mobile office; with Gao Yue, grand preceptor, Han Gui, minister of education, Liu Feng, grand commander, and others he attacked Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan and diverted the Wei River to flood the city.

literal: Ninth month, on yiyou day, Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yiyou day, Xiao Yan sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Tenth month of winter, on wushen day, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, set up Xiao Yan's younger brother's son Prince Zhengde of Linhe as ruler, and attacked Jiankang.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on wushen day, Hou Jing crossed the Yangzi, set up Prince Zhengde of Linhe, a nephew of Xiao Yan, as ruler, and attacked Jiankang.

literal: That year Koguryo, Shiwei, Rouran, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Koguryo, Shiwei, Rouran, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.

literal: [24] Spring, first month of the seventh year, on wuchen day, Xiao Yan's younger brother's son Xiao Zhengbiao, regional inspector of North Xuzhou and Marquis of Fengshan, submitted Zhongli; he was enfeoffed Duke of Lanling commandery with open state and Prince of Wu commandery.
idiomatic: [24] In the first month of spring in the seventh year, on wuchen day, Xiao Zhengbiao, a nephew of Xiao Yan, regional inspector of North Xuzhou and marquis of Fengshan, submitted Zhongli and was enfeoffed duke of Lanling commandery with open state and prince of Wu commandery.

literal: Third month, on dingmao day, Hou Jing took Jiankang and again set up Xiao Yan as ruler.
idiomatic: In the third month, on dingmao day, Hou Jing took Jiankang and again set up Xiao Yan as ruler.

literal: Xiao Yan's younger brother's son Zhi, regional inspector of North Yanzhou and Marquis of Dingxiang, and Tui, Marquis of Xiangtan, came to surrender.
idiomatic: Zhi, a nephew of Xiao Yan, regional inspector of North Yanzhou and marquis of Dingxiang, and Tui, marquis of Xiangtan, came to surrender.

literal: All commanderies and states north of the Yangzi in Xiao Yan's realm submitted.
idiomatic: All commanderies and states north of the Yangzi in Xiao Yan's realm submitted.

literal: Fourth month of summer: Grand Mobile Office Murong Shaozong and Grand Commander Liu Feng met a violent storm and drowned.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Grand Mobile Office Murong Shaozong and Grand Commander Liu Feng met a violent storm and drowned.

literal: On jiachen day an edict made Prince of Qi Wenxiang chancellor and Prince of Qi, with green sash and ribbon, praise at bowing without naming him, no quick step on entering court, sword and shoes in the hall, and fief over five commanderies of Ji and Ying provinces totaling one hundred fifty thousand households; the rest remained as before.
idiomatic: On jiachen day an edict made Prince of Qi Wenxiang chancellor and prince of Qi, with green sash and ribbon, praise at bowing without naming him, no quick step in court, sword and shoes in the hall, and fief over five Ji and Ying commanderies totaling one hundred fifty thousand households; all else stood unchanged.

literal: The prince firmly declined.
idiomatic: The prince firmly declined.

literal: That month Hou Jing killed Xiao Yan and set up his son Gang as ruler.
idiomatic: That month Hou Jing killed Xiao Yan and set up his son Gang as ruler.

literal: Fifth month: Prince of Qi Wenxiang led troops from Ye to Yingchuan.
idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince of Qi Wenxiang led troops from Ye to Yingchuan.

literal: Sixth month, on bingshen day, Ying province was taken; Baoju's grand general, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, eastern-route grand mobile office, and Duke of Taiyuan commandery with open state Wang Sizheng, Ying provincial inspector Huangfu Sengxian, and others were captured, together with more than ten thousand fighting men and tens of thousands of men and women.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingshen day, Ying province fell; Wang Sizheng, Baoju's grand general, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, eastern-route grand mobile office, and duke of Taiyuan commandery with open state, Huangfu Sengxian, Ying provincial inspector, and others were captured with more than ten thousand fighting men and tens of thousands of civilians.

literal: Prince of Qi Wenxiang then went to Luo province.
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Wenxiang then went to Luo province.

literal: Tenth month of winter, on guiwei day, Tan, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies with open office and Prince of Xianyang, was made grand preceptor.
idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on guiwei day, Tan, equal in honor to the three excellencies with open office and prince of Xianyang, was made grand preceptor.

literal: On jiawu day Pan Xiangle, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies with open office, was made minister of works.
idiomatic: On jiawu day Pan Xiangle, equal in honor to the three excellencies with open office, was made minister of works.

literal: Twelfth month, on jiachen day, Prince of Wu commandery Xiao Zhengbiao died.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen day, Prince of Wu commandery Xiao Zhengbiao died.

literal: On jiyou day Peng Yue, regional inspector of Bing province, was made minister of education.
idiomatic: On jiyou day Peng Yue, regional inspector of Bing province, was made minister of education.

literal: That year Rouran, Dudouyu, Shiwei, Koguryo, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: That year Rouran, Dudouyu, Shiwei, Koguryo, and Tuyuhun all sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Spring, first month of the eighth year, on xinyou day, the emperor held mourning for Prince of Qi Wenxiang in the Eastern Hall.
idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the eighth year, on xinyou day, the emperor held mourning for Prince of Qi Wenxiang in the Eastern Hall.

literal: On dingmao day an edict posthumously granted Prince of Qi Wenxiang the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the rites of the Nine Bestowals; his posthumous title was Prince Wenxiang.
idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict posthumously granted Prince of Qi Wenxiang the yellow battle-axe, commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, the Qi prince's seal and sash, the imperial carriage with curved canopy, yellow roof, left banner, front and rear feathered parasols, drum and pipe music, light chariots and armored escorts, and the rites of the nine bestowals; his posthumous title was Prince Wenxiang.

literal: On wuchen day an edict made the Prince of Qi commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and Prince of Qi commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.
idiomatic: On wuchen day an edict made the prince of Qi commissioner with full powers, chancellor, commander of all military affairs within and without, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, grand mobile office, and prince of Qi commandery, with a fief of ten thousand households.

literal: On jiaxu day Dudouyu and Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day Dudouyu and Khitan both sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Second month, on jiashen day, Prince of Qi Wenxiang was buried; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.
idiomatic: In the second month, on jiashen day, Prince of Qi Wenxiang was buried; the imperial carriage farewelled him on the Zhang bank.

literal: On gengyin day Gao Longzhi, director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand preceptor.
idiomatic: On gengyin day Gao Longzhi, director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand preceptor.

literal: Third month, on gengshen day, the Prince of Qi commandery was advanced in rank to Prince of Qi.
idiomatic: In the third month, on gengshen day, the prince of Qi commandery was advanced in rank to prince of Qi.

literal: Fourth month of summer, on yisi day, Rouran sent envoys with tribute.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yisi day, Rouran sent envoys with tribute.

literal: Fifth month, on jiayin day, an edict made the Prince of Qi chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with fief over ten commanderies of Ji, Ying, and Ding provinces totaling two hundred thousand households and the full rites of the Nine Bestowals;
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, an edict made the prince of Qi chancellor, overall director of the hundred affairs, with fief over ten Ji, Ying, and Ding commanderies totaling two hundred thousand households and the full rites of the nine bestowals;

literal: the Qi state's grand consort was made queen mother and the princess consort was made queen.
idiomatic: the Qi state's grand consort was made queen mother and the princess consort was made queen.

literal: On bingchen day an edict returned the imperial throne to the state of Qi; that same day he abdicated to a separate palace.
idiomatic: On bingchen day an edict returned the imperial throne to the state of Qi; that same day he abdicated to a separate palace.

literal: The emperor loved literature and had handsome bearing.
idiomatic: The emperor loved literature and had handsome bearing.

literal: His strength could lift stone lions over a wall; in shooting nothing missed.
idiomatic: He could lift stone lions over a wall; in archery he never missed.

literal: At festive gatherings on auspicious days he often ordered the ministers to compose poetry; easy and grave in manner, he had the manner of Emperor Xiaowen.
idiomatic: At festive gatherings on auspicious days he often had ministers compose poetry; calm and grave in manner, he had something of Emperor Xiaowen's style.

literal: When Prince of Qi Wenxiang succeeded to affairs he greatly resented this; he made Grand General Central Army Staff Member Cui Jishu a secretariat yellow gate attendant and ordered him to watch the emperor's movements; large and small all had to be known to Jishu.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Wenxiang took power he deeply resented this; he made Cui Jishu, staff member of the grand general's central army, a secretariat yellow gate attendant to watch the emperor's every move, great and small alike.

literal: Wenxiang wrote Jishu: "How does the fool compare now?
idiomatic: Wenxiang wrote Jishu: "How is the fool now?

literal: Has the fool's condition improved a little?"
idiomatic: Has his condition improved a little?"

literal: The emperor once hunted east of Ye, galloping in pursuit like flight.
idiomatic: The emperor once hunted east of Ye at a gallop.

literal: Supervising Guard Commissioner Wunaluo Shougongfa called from behind: "Son of Heaven, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"
idiomatic: Guard commissioner Wunaluo Shougongfa called from behind: "Son of Heaven, do not gallop—the Grand General will be angry!"

literal: Wenxiang once attended drinking, raised a great cup, and urged the emperor: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."
idiomatic: Wenxiang once raised a great cup at drink and urged the emperor: "Your servant Cheng urges Your Majesty to drink."

literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "From antiquity there has been no state that did not perish—what use is this life to me!"
idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said: "From antiquity no state failed to perish—what use is this life to me!"

literal: Wenxiang raged: "Imperial We!"
idiomatic: Wenxiang raged: "Imperial We!"

literal: Imperial We!"
idiomatic: Imperial We!"

literal: Dog-foot imperial We!"
idiomatic: Dog-foot imperial We!"

literal: He had Jishu strike the emperor three blows with the fist and flung his robes and went out.
idiomatic: He had Jishu strike the emperor three blows and stormed out.

literal: The next day Wenxiang sent Jishu to console the emperor; the emperor also apologized.
idiomatic: The next day Wenxiang sent Jishu to console the emperor; the emperor also apologized.

literal: Silk was granted; Jishu did not dare accept and reported to Wenxiang; Wenxiang had him take one length.
idiomatic: Silk was granted; Jishu did not dare accept and reported to Wenxiang, who had him take one length.

literal: The emperor bound a hundred lengths and gave them to him, saying: "That too is only one length!"
idiomatic: The emperor bound a hundred lengths and gave them to him, saying: "That too is only one length!"

literal: Unable to bear worry and insult, the emperor chanted Xie Lingyun's poem: "When Han perished Zifang rose; the Qin emperor was shamed before Lu Lian.
idiomatic: Unable to bear insult, the emperor chanted Xie Lingyun: "When Han perished Zifang rose; the Qin emperor was shamed before Lu Lian.

literal: Originally men of rivers and seas—loyalty and righteousness move gentlemen."
idiomatic: Men of rivers and seas—loyalty and righteousness move gentlemen."

literal: Regular Attendant and Lecturing Attendant Xun Ji knew the emperor's mind; with Prince of Huashan Daqi and Yuan Jin he secretly plotted, building a hill within the palace and digging a tunnel toward the north city.
idiomatic: Regular attendant and lecturing attendant Xun Ji read the emperor's mind; with Prince Daqi of Huashan and Yuan Jin he secretly built a hill in the palace and dug a tunnel toward the north city.

literal: At Qianqiu Gate the gatekeeper heard underground noise and reported to Wenxiang.
idiomatic: At Qianqiu Gate the gatekeeper heard underground noise and reported to Wenxiang.

literal: Wenxiang led troops into the palace and said: "Your Majesty, what do you mean by rebelling!
idiomatic: Wenxiang led troops into the palace and said: "Your Majesty, what do you mean by rebelling!

literal: Your servant father and son have merit preserving the altars of soil and grain—how have we failed Your Majesty!
idiomatic: My father and I preserved the altars—how have we failed you!

literal: He was about to kill the consorts.
idiomatic: He was about to kill the consorts.

literal: The emperor said sternly: "You yourself wish to rebel—what has that to do with me.
idiomatic: The emperor said sternly: "You mean to rebel yourself—what has that to do with me.

literal: I do not spare even my own person—how much more consorts!"
idiomatic: I spare not even my own person—how much more consorts!"

literal: Wenxiang left the couch, kowtowed, and wept loudly begging pardon.
idiomatic: Wenxiang left the couch, kowtowed, and wept for pardon.

literal: Then they drank heavily; only late at night did he go out.
idiomatic: Then they drank heavily until late at night before he left.

literal: After three days he imprisoned the emperor in the Hall of Blended Splendor; Daqi, Jin, and the others were all boiled alive in the market.
idiomatic: Three days later he imprisoned the emperor in the Hall of Blended Splendor; Daqi, Jin, and the others were all boiled alive in the market.

literal: When the throne was about to be yielded to Prince Wenxuan, Xu of Xiangcheng and Minister of Works Pan Xiangle, Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhang Liang, Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhao Yanchen, and others asked to enter with reports.
idiomatic: When the throne was to be yielded to Prince Wenxuan, Xu of Xiangcheng, Pan Xiangle, minister of works, Zhang Liang, attendant-in-ordinary, Zhao Yanchen, yellow gate gentleman, and others asked to enter with reports.

literal: The emperor received them in Zhaoyang Hall; Xu said: "The Five Phases pass in turn; there is beginning and there is end.
idiomatic: The emperor received them in Zhaoyang Hall. Xu said: "The Five Phases pass in turn; there is beginning and there is end.

literal: The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him.
idiomatic: The prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him.

literal: We, risking death, hear and report: may Your Majesty yield as Yao yielded to Shun."
idiomatic: We, risking death, hear and report: may Your Majesty yield as Yao yielded to Shun."

literal: The emperor composed his face and answered: "This matter has been deferred long; I shall respectfully yield and withdraw."
idiomatic: The emperor composed his face and said: "This matter has been deferred long; I shall respectfully yield and withdraw."

literal: He also said: "If so, an imperial order must be drafted."
idiomatic: He also said: "If so, an imperial order must be drafted."

literal: Gentlemen of the Secretariat Cui Shao and Pei Rangzhi reported: "The order is already drafted."
idiomatic: Secretariat gentlemen Cui Shao and Pei Rangzhi reported: "The order is already drafted."

literal: It was at once given to Yang Yin, who presented it to the emperor—ten articles in all.
idiomatic: It was at once given to Yang Yin, who presented it to the emperor—ten articles in all.
